overall: Atlanta is starting the morning cool at 64.4°F with mostly clear skies (12% cloud fraction) and light winds, well below the 87°F NWS text forecast high. The overnight running max of 69.8°F occurred anomalously at 01:40 ET — likely brief boundary-layer mixing from northwest winds — and temperatures have since cooled back, leaving a clean slate for daytime heating. Skies are mostly clear ahead of what should be a sunny day, but the pace of warming will be the key variable.
forecast_obs_notes: There is a notable and significant divergence between the NWS text forecast (87°F) and the NWP model suite: ECMWF=80.9°F, HRRR=83.2°F, and NBM=80.1°F all cluster roughly 4–7°F below the official forecast. The D1_NOW ensemble resolves this by landing at 84–85°F as its dominant bucket (57.6% probability), suggesting the calibrated model sees some additional warming potential beyond raw NWP output but still well short of the NWS narrative high.
max_temp_prediction: The ensemble model delivers an unusually high-confidence signal — 84–85°F at 57.6% (Tier 1) with a 33.4-point gap over the next bucket — pointing to a daily high in the mid-80s. Raw NWP consensus (~81–83°F) provides the lower anchor, while NWS's 87°F likely reflects mesoscale heating potential that the global models partially underresolve; the calibrated D1_NOW splitting the difference at ~84–85°F is the most defensible estimate. Confidence is moderately high given model agreement on direction, with residual uncertainty driven by how aggressively the boundary layer mixes under light east winds and how quickly NW-advected drier air supports solar heating.
